page: Microsoft Azure E32-16s_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the ESv3 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8272CL x86_64 processor operating at 2.6 GHz, configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high resource density of 16.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Local storage is provided via a bundled 524 GB SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core execution. Single-core metrics, including stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores, fall into the weak category. However, multi-core benchmarks, such as stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU scores, achieve average tier results. Memory bandwidth tests, including uncached read and write operations, also register in the average range.

The high memory-to-vCPU ratio makes this server suitable for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high single-threaded compute performance. Database operations, such as Redis SET operations which benchmarked at an average 12.39 million operations per second, and static web serving at 11.08 GB/sec, are appropriate use cases. The hardware configuration presents a tradeoff of high memory capacity and local SSD storage against lower single-core processing speeds, making it less optimal for compute-bound or single-threaded tasks.
